build: Sprint 6 — team invites + roles, gates G3–G5 (client only)
note: G1 + G2 shipped 2026-08-01 and are not re-litigated here. The whole server half of G3, G4 and G5 already exists (api/team.ts, api/invites.ts); every feature below is UI against routes that are already live and already tested by G2's 59 exit assertions.

features.title: Select primitive
features.description: Native <select> styled to match Input, wired to Field context for id/aria-describedby/aria-invalid/aria-required. Native rather than Radix: role pickers are 2-3 options, and native gets mobile pickers and keyboard type-ahead for free.
steps: Renders inside a Field and the label's htmlFor resolves to the select (clicking the label focuses it)
Field error state paints the invalid border and sets aria-invalid on the select
Options render from an `options` prop; the selected value is controlled and onChange fires with the new value
disabled renders greyed with cursor-not-allowed and cannot be changed by keyboard
FAILURE CASE: used standalone with no Field, it falls back to the caller's own id/aria-* rather than throwing
features.notes: Verified in-browser on /design-system: Field supplies the id, aria-describedby switches hint->error, aria-invalid set only when invalid, placeholder and per-option disabled both work.

features.title: Team API client + types
features.description: services/team.ts over apiRequest for all eight routes, plus ProjectMember / PendingInvite / MembersResponse / InvitePreview types mirroring api/team.ts and api/invites.ts response shapes.
steps: teamAPI.members(slug) returns { members, invites, canManage } with ISO date strings
teamAPI.invite() returns inviteUrl on 201 and throws a typed ApiError carrying status 409 when the address is already a member
teamAPI.removeMember / setRole / transferOwnership / revokeInvite each hit the documented path and method
invitesAPI.preview(token) and invitesAPI.accept(token) hit /api/invites, NOT /api/projects/:slug (T-D2)
FAILURE CASE: a 403 from setRole on the owner's row surfaces the server's message verbatim, not 'Request failed (403)'
features.notes: Verified against the running API — 409 (already a member) and 403/410 all surface the server message verbatim.

features.title: useMembers hook
features.description: Loads the roster, exposes canManage, and owns the mutations so the page stays presentational. Refetches after every mutation rather than patching local state — role and ownership changes have server-side side effects (T-D4, T-D5) the client cannot reproduce.
steps: Loads on mount keyed on slug; switching slug re-loads rather than showing the previous project's roster
canManage comes from the server response, not from a locally inferred role
A failed mutation leaves the roster unchanged and surfaces the message
FAILURE CASE: hook called with slug === undefined does not fetch and does not throw
features.notes: Verified: roster reloads after every mutation; the leave path skips the refetch, which would 404 on the way out.

features.title: Members tab + /p/:slug/members route
features.description: Member rows (avatar, name, email, role, joined), pending-invite list for owner/admin only, and the Members entry in ProjectTabs.
steps: /p/:slug/members renders the roster with the owner first
Signed in as a `member`, the pending-invite section is absent entirely (not just disabled) — the server sends invites: []
The Members tab appears in ProjectTabs for every role
Loading shows a skeleton, and a project the caller cannot see shows the not-found surface rather than an empty table
FAILURE CASE: a project with exactly one member (the owner) renders that one row and no empty state
features.notes: Verified as owner (3 roles rendered, owner first) and as a plain member (no invite button, no Selects, no pending-invite section at all).

features.title: Invite dialog with copy-once link
features.description: Email + role, POST, then the returned inviteUrl shown once with a Copy button and an explicit 'this is the only time you will see this' warning — the same treatment the ingest key gets.
steps: Submitting a valid address returns a link that appears in the dialog with a Copy button
Closing and reopening the dialog does NOT show the previous link again
A 409 (already a member) shows the server's message next to the field and does not close the dialog
A 429 (rate limit, 20/hr per project) shows the server's message rather than a generic failure
FAILURE CASE: an empty or malformed email is rejected client-side before the request, and the button stays disabled
features.notes: Verified: link shown once, reopening the dialog shows a blank form, 409 keeps the dialog open with the server message.

features.title: Inline role editing + invite revoke
features.description: Per-row role Select for owner/admin, and a Revoke action on each pending invite.
steps: Changing a member's role from the row Select persists and the roster re-sorts (admins above members)
The owner's row Select is disabled with a hint pointing at transfer-ownership (T-D3)
As an admin, attempting the owner's row is impossible in the UI and 403s at the API if forced
Revoking a pending invite removes it from the list
FAILURE CASE: a role change that fails leaves the Select showing the OLD role, not the attempted one
features.notes: Verified: role change persisted and re-sorted the roster; owner row renders a Badge with no control; revoke removed the pending invite.

features.title: /invite/:token accept screen
features.description: Preview then accept. Lives under ProtectedRoute but outside AppLayout — an invitee may have zero projects, so the workspace chrome has nothing to render.
steps: Signed out, /invite/:token bounces to /login and returns to the same invite URL after signing in
Signed in as the invited address, the screen names the project, the inviter and the offered role, and Accept joins then lands on the project
Signed in as a DIFFERENT address, the wrong-email state renders before any accept attempt (emailMatches: false) and names which address the invite was sent to
An expired, revoked or already-accepted token renders the dead-link state (410) with 'ask your teammate for a new link'
FAILURE CASE: a garbage token renders not-found (404), not a crash or an infinite spinner
features.notes: All four states verified in-browser — signed-out bounce to /login and back, happy-path accept landing on /p/test/issues, wrong-address, 410 dead link, 404 garbage token.

features.title: invite notification in the bell
features.description: NotificationKind gains 'invite'; the bell renders it with its own icon and copy. It deliberately does NOT navigate — accepting requires the token, which is never stored, so there is no in-app destination.
steps: An invite notification renders with the person-add icon, distinct from the regression icon
Clicking it marks it read and does NOT navigate to /p/:slug/* (the recipient is not a member yet and would 404)
A regression notification still navigates to its issue — no regression in the existing behaviour
FAILURE CASE: an invite notification for a project the user later joined still renders without throwing on the null issueId
features.notes: Known gap, named not hidden: the bell cannot offer an Accept button because the token is not in the row. The real fix is GET /api/invites/mine (authenticated by email, no token) — a backend addition, out of G4's scope. | Verified: the invite row renders with its own icon and the follow-up hint, and clicking it marks read without navigating. Regression rows still navigate.

features.title: Leave project
features.description: Self-removal from the Members page via ConfirmDialog. DELETE /:slug/members/:selfId is the same route as removal — the server already distinguishes self.
steps: A non-owner member sees Leave project; confirming lands them on /projects and the project is gone from the list
The owner sees Leave disabled with the reason (transfer first) — the server 409s, and the UI should say so before the click
Cancelling the dialog leaves membership intact
FAILURE CASE: a 409 from the server still surfaces its message rather than silently navigating away
features.notes: Verified: left the project, landed on /projects, project gone from the list. Owner sees the disabled explanation instead.

features.title: Remove member
features.description: Row action for owner/admin, behind ConfirmDialog that names T-D5's blast radius: their tickets get unassigned with a system comment, and their notifications for this project are deleted.
steps: Removing a member drops the row and the roster count
The dialog states the ticket-unassignment consequence before the click, not after
The response's ticketsUnassigned count is surfaced when non-zero
The owner's row offers no Remove action at all (409 territory)
FAILURE CASE: removing yourself through this path routes to the Leave flow's navigation, not a stale roster
features.notes: Verified including the ticket count — removing a member with one assigned ticket reported "1 ticket unassigned".

features.title: Transfer ownership
features.description: Owner-only. Select over existing members (T-D4: the target must already be a member), behind ConfirmDialog — the one action in the product the actor cannot undo alone.
steps: Only the owner sees the transfer control; an admin does not
The Select lists existing members excluding the owner themselves
Confirming transfers, and the page re-renders with the caller now shown as admin and the owner-only controls gone
The dialog says plainly that this cannot be undone without the new owner's cooperation
FAILURE CASE: with no other members, the transfer control explains why it is unavailable instead of opening an empty Select
features.notes: Verified end to end: transfer flipped the roster, the caller re-rendered as admin with owner-only controls gone, and Project.ownerId + the owner member row agree (T-D4).

features.title: Select in the design-system showcase
features.description: Add Select to the Form kit section of /design-system and update the form-kit status comment in the design-system index, which currently lists Select as unbuilt.
steps: /design-system renders a working Select in the Form kit section
The 'STILL UNBUILT' comment in components/design-system/index.ts no longer names Select
FAILURE CASE: the showcase Select is interactive, not a dead render
features.notes: Verified on /design-system — two live Selects, one valid one showing the error state.
